sections.title: And it came to pass that Baruch was forsaken.

verses.text: And Jeremiah said to Pasher, “You have caused the people to forsake righteousness, both in your time and in the generations that follow after your fathers and your children.”

Indeed, they have committed exceedingly grievous sins, far worse than those of your fathers. They have sold that which is of no value; they have caused sickness to be forgotten; they have brought forth iniquity to be judged.
The children of Israel shall receive the price of the great sacrifice, thirty pieces of silver; and that silver shall be given as the price of a potter's field.
Therefore, as the Lord has commanded me, so will I speak.
Thus, they have shed innocent blood, and judgment and destruction shall come upon them; and it shall descend upon their children after them.
And concerning the matter that Baruch spoke in Babylon, this is what remains.
And it came to pass, when the king of the Chaldeans took the children of Israel captive, that the Lord spoke to Jeremiah.

And He said, “My beloved Jeremiah, arise and depart from this city; for I will destroy it because of the multitude of the iniquities of the people that dwell therein; therefore, you and Baruch, go forth.”
Your prayer is as a strong fortress in the midst of the city, and around it is as a wall of defense; now arise and depart, lest the army of the Chaldeans come upon you and the land be laid waste.
And Jeremiah spoke, saying, “O Lord, I am afraid; let Your servant speak before You.”
And the Lord said, “O my beloved Jeremiah! Speak.”

And Jeremiah spoke, saying, “O Lord, who dost purchase all, shall the king be delivered into the hand of his army, and shall I be cast out of the city which Thou hast chosen, and shall I be delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans?”
“O Lord, let it not be so; for I am in Thy hand, destroy me not.”
And the Lord said unto Jeremiah, “I will consume the iniquity of the people that dwell therein; and thou, O my beloved, arise, thou and Baruch, and go forth.”
“For I had previously declared that if I did not break down her walls, neither the king nor his army could enter into her land.”
“Now arise, and go unto Baruch; and declare unto him all these words; and at the sixth hour of the night, arise and go unto the gate of the city.”
“I will show you; for I had previously declared that if I did not destroy the city, they would not be able to enter therein.”
And the Lord spoke these words, and Jeremiah departed.
And then Jeremiah girded his loins; and he put on a sackcloth upon himself, and entered into the house of the Lord.

And Baruch also girded himself with sackcloth upon his loins, and when he saw Jeremiah, he said, “O my father Jeremiah, what has befallen thee? What sin hath the people committed?” And he lifted up his voice and cried.
The people were in distress at that time, for Jeremiah was mourning, and he himself was in sorrow; and he prayed for the people until they were delivered from their troubles.
And Baruch asked, "My father Jeremiah, what has befallen you?" And Jeremiah answered, "Let us not tear our garments, but let us rend our hearts."
"From this day forward, let these people not be forgiven, until we weep for them; for it is fitting that we should lament and not add water to the cisterns," he said.
And Baruch said, "My father Jeremiah, what has befallen you?"
Jeremiah said, "The Lord will deliver the city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and He will cause the people to be led astray by evil."
And Baruch, having heard all these words, tore his garments and said, "My father Jeremiah, what shall I do for you?"
Jeremiah said, "To know the matter in truth, remain with me from the night until the sixth hour."
And they sat in the temple, and at the time when it was the sixth hour of the night, the Lord spoke to Jeremiah to go forth.
He went out with Baruch, and they arrived at the scroll; and they sat down while they prayed.
And the sound of the cherubim was heard; and angels came down from heaven, holding in their hands the flames of fire, and they stood by the scroll.
And it came to pass that Jeremiah and Baruch said, "Concerning this matter, a sign shall indeed be found today, as it is true."
And Jeremiah said, "I beseech you, let not the city be destroyed until we believe in the Lord." Thus he spoke to the angels.
And the Lord said, "Until you converse with my beloved Jeremiah, do not destroy the city." Thus He spoke to the angels.
And Jeremiah then said, "O my Lord, I beseech You; let me speak with You, for I am troubled." And the Lord said, "O my beloved Jeremiah, speak of that which you love."
And Jeremiah said, "O my Lord, deliver this city from the hand of its enemy, as You have given it into the hand of Babylon's people; behold, today I know."
"What shall I do for those who have been taken captive, for they are Your holy ones? What shall I do for them, that You may love them?"

And the Lord said, "Take them and give them to the land; for you, O land, were created upon the waters, and upon the seven heavens, you were established. Hearken to the word of the Lord, and receive your glory; and until your beloved comes, keep your wealth."

And Jeremiah spoke thus, saying, "O my Lord, I beseech You; the people have long awaited their deliverance, and I, Your servant Jeremiah, am more in need of deliverance than all the people of my land, for I seek to deliver the Ethiopian, Abimelech."
"He has drawn me out of the pit of destruction; I do not wish to see the ruin of the city."
And the Lord said to Jeremiah, "Send Abimelech to this mountain path, and until the people return to their land, I will be with you."
And you, Jeremiah, go to the land of Babylon until you arrive, and go to Egypt with the people, and until they return to their land, instruct them to shine.
But Baruch remained there in Jerusalem; and the Lord spoke all these things to Jeremiah, and Jeremiah went up to heaven.
And Baruch and Jeremiah entered the temple; and all the vessels that they were to serve with, the Lord commanded them to give to the earth; and the earth then received them.

Both of them sat down and wept; and in the evening, Jeremiah sent Abimelech, saying, “Take your cloak and go to the place of Agrippa, on the road that leads to the mountain; for the Lord's help, and His lordship has been placed upon you, so bring a little silver for the poor.”
And he went as he was commanded; and in the evening, the Chaldean army besieged the city; and the great angel blew the trumpet.
And he said, “The Chaldean army, enter; behold, they shall open the gates for you.”
At that time, the king went with his army and besieged all the people.
At that time, Jeremiah took the key of the temple and went out of the city to the outside.
And this key he held, saying, “Sun, receive the key of the house of the Lord,” and he cast it before the sun.
“Our sins we have been bearing since we were born, and it is not fitting for us to keep Him to protect Him, for the Lord will keep His word until you speak it until many generations come,” he said.
And Jeremiah, as he lamented for his people, wept; and they took him along with the people, even unto Babylon.
But Baruch, being weary, was heavy upon himself; he sat down and wept; and he said this:
“It is for the sin of the people that they have been forsaken; what is the reason for the ruin of Jerusalem?”

Let it not be said that we have held the city of our God by our own strength, for it has fallen into the hands of its enemies because of the sins of the people and our own iniquities; it is not by their power that it has fallen.
It is because of our sins that you have been given over; however, it is not by your strength that you have been able to hold this city.
Our God has indeed delivered us; He shall return us to our land; but for you, there is no strength remaining.
They have departed from this world, and we have not seen the destruction of this city; for our forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, are righteous.
And after he had spoken this, he went out weeping, saying, “O Jerusalem, for thee I mourn.”
And he departed from the city and went to the house of mourning; and the angels were coming to comfort him in all things.

And Abimelech sent Jeremiah from the place where he had been, and he brought forth a letter; and he found a wilderness that was desolate, and he lay down under a solitary tree; and he took his rest for six years, and he did not awaken from his sleep.
And after that time, he arose from his sleep, and said, "Surely my soul shall be honored, for I have not forsaken my sleep, and I shall lie down again for a little while."
And he broke forth from his slumber, and his slumber was renewed, and as he lay down, he found himself heavy with sleep, and he did not forsake his rest, and he lay down again.

Thus he spoke, saying, "I fear that I shall not lie down again nor shall I be at rest; for my father Jeremiah has been troubled and has sent me forth with a sword, and I fear that he shall not be angry with me."
For it has become hot, and there is no time for rest; therefore, I shall arise now and go forth."
And he arose, taking the letter with him, and entered into the city of Jerusalem. And he did not know the city nor his house.
A great stone has come upon me, and he said, "O Lord, Thou art he who has called me."

Thus he spoke, saying, "Is this city not Jerusalem? For I have come to the way of the mountain, and I have become heavy with sleep, and I have not forsaken my rest; and I wonder if perhaps my mind shall be troubled."
"How shall I speak of this matter to Jeremiah, as if the city has become as it was?" And Jerusalem sought all the signs that were in the city.
And he returned again to the city; and he desired to know what was there; but he found it not; and he said, "A great stone has come upon me; O Lord, Thou art he who has called me."
ሁለተኛም ከከተማ ርቆ ወጣ፤ እያዘነም ተቀመጠ፤ ሲሄድም አያውቅም ነበር፤ የበለሱንም ሙዳይ አኖረ፤ “ይህን ድንቁርና እግዚአብሔር ከእኔ እስኪያርቅልኝ ድረስ በዚህ እቀመጣለሁ” አለ።
ከዚህ በኋላ ተቀምጦ ሳለ አንድ ሽማግሌ ሰው ከምድረ በዳ ሲመለስ አየ።
አቤሜሌክም እንዲህ አለ፥ “አንተ ሽማግሌ፥ ይቺ ከተማ ማን ናት? ብዬ እጠይቅሃለሁ።”
ያም ሽማግሌ፥ “ኢየሩሳሌም ናት” አለው፤ “ያገኘሁት ሰው የለምና የእግዚአብሔር ካህን ኤርምያስ ወዴት አለ? ሌዋዊው ባሮክና የከተማው ሕዝብ ሁሉስ ወዴት አሉ?” አለው፤
ሽማግሌውም እንዲህ አለው፥ “አንተ ከዚች ከተማ አይደለህምን? ይህን ያህል ዘመን ኖረህ የእርሱን ነገር ትጠይቅ ዘንድ ኤርምያስን ዛሬ ማን ዐሰበው?
ተማርኮ በባቢሎን ንጉሥ በናቡከደነፆር እጅ ተሰጥቶአልና፤ እስራኤልንም ያስተምር ዘንድ ወደ ባቢሎን ሄዶአልና ኤርምያስስ ከሕዝቡ ጋር በባቢሎን አለ።”
አቤሜሌክም ያንጊዜ ከዚያ ከሽማግሌው ይህን ቃል ሰማ።
አቤሜሌክም እንዲህ አለው፥ “ሰውን፥ ይልቁንም ሽማግሌውን ሰው ሊንቁት አይገባም እንጂ አንተ ሽማግሌ ሰው ባትሆን በሰደብሁህ ነበር፤ በአንተም በዘበትሁብህ ነበር፤ ያም ባይሆን አእምሮውን ያጣ ሽማግሌ ብዬ በሰደብሁህ ነበር።
ሕዝቡ ተማርከው ወደ ባቢሎን ሄዱ፤ ስለምትለውስ ነገር የሰማይ ሻሻቴ እንኳ በእነርሱ ላይ ቢወርድ ወደ ባቢሎን ተማርከው ይሄዱ ዘንድ ጊዜው አይደለም።
አንተ ግን ተማርከው ወደ ባቢሎን ሄዱ ትላለህ፤ በሕዝቡ ዘንድ ላሉ ለበሽተኞች እንሰጥ ዘንድ አባቴ ኤርምያስ እኔን እንደ ላከኝ ጥቂት በለስ ላመጣ ወደ አግሪጳስ ወይን ቦታ ሄድሁ።
ሄጄም ከዚያ ደረስሁ፤ ያዘዘኝንም ይዤ ተመለስሁ፤ ስሄድም አንዲት ዛፍ አገኘሁ፤ የቀትር ጊዜ ነበርና በበታችዋ ዐርፍ ዘንድ ተቀመጥሁ።
ከዚያም የበለሱን ሙዳይ ተንተርሼ ተኛሁ፤ ከእንቅልፌም በነቃሁ ጊዜ የዘገየሁ መሰለኝ፤ የበለሱንም ሙዳይ ከፍቼ አየሁ፤ መርጬ እንደለቀምኋቸው ወተቱ ሲፈስስ አገኘሁት።
እነሆ፥ አንተ ሕዝቡ ተማርከው ወደ ባቢሎን ሄዱ ትላለህ፤ እነሆ፥ በለሱ እንዳልጠወለገ እይ” ብሎ የበለሱን ሙዳይ ከፍቶ አሳየው።
ሽማግሌውም በለሱ አዲስ እንደ ሆነ፥ ወተቱም እንደሚፈስስ አየ፤ ያንጊዜም ሽማግሌው አደነቀ።
አቤሜሌክንም እንዲህ አለው፥ “ልጄ፥ አንተ ደግ ሰው ነህ፤ ፈጣሪህ የዚህችን ከተማ ጥፋት ሊያሳይህ አልወደደምና አምላክ ለአንተ መረጋጋትን አምጥቶ አድኖሃል።
እነሆ፥ ሕዝቡ ወደ ባቢሎን ተማርከው ከሄዱ ዛሬ ስድሳ ስድስት ዓመት ሆነ።
ልጄ፥ ፈጽመህ ልታውቅስ ከወደድህ ዘሮችዋ እንደ በቀሉ ወደ እርሻዎች ፈጽመህ ተመልከት፤ የበለስም ጊዜው አይደለም፤” ያንጊዜ አቤሜሌክ የዚህ ሁሉ ጊዜው እንዳልሆነ ዐወቀ።
ቃሉንም አሰምቶ፥ “የሰማይና የምድር አምላክ፥ በሀገሩ ሁሉ ያሉ የጻድቃን ነፍሳት ዕረፍታቸው የሆንህ ጌታዬና አምላኬ ሆይ፥ አመሰግንሃለሁ፥” አለ።
ሽማግሌውንም፥ “ይህ ወር ምንድን ነው?” አለው፤ እርሱም፦ የኔሳን ወር ዐሥራ ሁለተኛው ቀን፥ ይኸውም ሚያዝያ ነው” አለው።
ከዚህም በኋላ አቤሜሌክ ለዚህ ሽማግሌ ከበለሶቹ ሰጠው፤ እርሱም፥ “አምላክ ወደ ሰማያዊት ሀገር ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ይምራህ” አለው።
And Abimelech arose and went out of the city, and after that he prayed unto the Lord.
Behold, an angel came and guided Baruch; and he found him sitting in the house of the tomb.
And when the greeting was given, they turned to one another and were confounded; for within their hearts, they lifted their eyes to heaven.

Thus he prayed, saying, “The God who gives reward to His beloved ones, to the righteous, is still present; O my soul, prepare thyself; for this is what thou sayest to thy holy dwelling, rejoice in this; and thy mourning shall return unto joy.”
And thereafter, the faithful shall come; and to thy rest shall they return; look unto the sanctuary and unto thy faith.

As thou art looking unto these things, know that it has been sixty years since they were taken; they have not perished; they have not been cast away; yet, behold, until this day they are still preserved.

Thou hast no sin, and the garment of the righteous is kept from the true angel, for thou hast kept the commandment given unto thee; thus shall my flesh do unto thee; and He shall keep thee again by His power.”

And Baruch, after he had prayed thus, Abimelech returned and said, “The Lord who has spoken concerning me to Jeremiah, to declare the words that we shall be carried away unto Babylon, let Him reveal unto us, that thou mayest arise and pray.”
And Baruch prayed, saying, “O mighty God, the light that proceeds from Thy mouth, I love Thee;
for Thy goodness I will seek; Thy name is still present; and there is none who can know Him by searching.”
በልቡናዬ ፈቃድህን ለማድረግ በደግነት የታወቅሁ እሆን ዘንድ፥ ለአገልጋይህ ለኤርምያስም ወደ ባቢሎን ጽፌ እልክ ዘንድ የኔን የባሪያህን ልመና ስማ።”
ይህንም ሲጸልይ መልአኩ መጥቶ ለባሮክ እንዲህ አለው፥ “ብሩህ ነገርን የምትመክር ባሮክ ሆይ፥ አንተ ወደ ኤርምያስ ትልክ ዘንድ ማንን እልካለሁ? ብለህ አታስብ።
ነገ ፀሐይ ሲወጣ ንስር ወደ አንተ ይመጣል፤ ወደ ኤርምያስም የምትልከውን ነገር አንተ መርምር፤ በመጽሐፍም ጻፍ።”
የእስራኤልን ልጆች እንዲህ በላቸው፥ “በእናንተ ዘንድ እንግዳ ሰው ቢኖር እስከ ዐሥራ አምስት ቀን ድረስ ከእናንተ ይለይ።
ከዚህም በኋላ ወደ ሀገራችሁ አገባችኋለሁ ይላል እግዚአብሔር፤ እስከ ዐሥራ አምስት ቀንም ድረስ ከባቢሎን ያልተለየ ሰው ቢኖር ኤርምያስ ወደ ከተማ ገብቶ በባቢሎን ያሉ እስራኤልን ይዝለፋቸው፤ ይላል እግዚአብሔር።”
ይህንም ከተናገረ በኋላ መልአኩ ከባሮክ ዘንድ ሄደ። ባሮክም እስከ አደባባዩ ድረስ ሸኘው፤ ወረቀትና ጥቁር ቀለምም አመጣ።
የእግዚአብሔር አገልጋዩ ባሮክ እንዲህ ብሎ ደብዳቤ ጻፈ፥ “ስለ ስድባችንና ስለ ጥፋታችን ያዘንን ሆነን እንወጣ ዘንድ ፈጣሪያችን አልተወንምና ወደ ባቢሎን ለተማረከው ለኤርምያስ ደስታና ሐሤት ይሁን።
ስለዚህ ነገር ጌታችን እንባችንን አይቶ አዘነልን፤ አስቀድሞ ለአባቶቻችን ለአብርሃምና ለይስሐቅ፥ ለያዕቆብም ያጸናውን ቃል ኪዳን ዐሰበ።
መልአኩንም ወደ እኔ ልኮ ወደ አንተ የላክሁብህን ነገሮች ነገረኝ።
“ከግብፅ ምድርና ከእሳት ቤቶች ያወጣን የእስራኤል አምላክ እግዚአብሔር ያደረጋቸው ነገሮች እኒህ ናቸው፤ ልቡናችሁን ከፍ ከፍ አደረጋችሁ፤ በፊቱም አንገታችሁን አደነደናችሁ እንጂ ሕጉን ሁሉ አልጠበቃችሁምና።

The Lord hath said, "Ye have not hearkened to the words of My servant Jeremiah, whom I sent unto you; but I have delivered you into the hand of Babylon. Yet those who have hearkened to My words, I will bring forth from Babylon; and they shall not dwell as strangers in Jerusalem."

"If thou desirest to know their way, let thy heart be steadfast; for the waters of the Jordan shall be their fate. Yet unto the man who hath not hearkened to this letter, there is a greater sign, a seal that is upon him."
And Baruch went forth from the house of the grave; and he said, "O Baruch, who dost teach faith, art thou not gracious?"
And Baruch said, "Thou art chosen from all the hosts of heaven, and in thine eyes is the light that hath been made known unto thee, and thou shalt speak."
"What dost thou come to do now?" he said. And he answered, "I have come hither to send thee all that thou lovest."
And Baruch said, "Canst thou deliver these things to Jeremiah and send them unto Babylon?" And he answered, "Thus have I been sent."
And Baruch wrote his letter; and thereafter he took the five measures of barley which Abimelech had given him, and he bound them upon the neck of his servant.
"O servant of all the hosts, go in peace and safety, and bring me tidings of their well-being," he said.
"Do not be dismayed by what Noah hath sent; do not turn back from returning unto him. Nevertheless, for Noah, three times did the word return unto him."

"Even so shall all good things be unto thee, that thou mayest be blessed; and let the things that are pleasing unto thee be sent unto Jeremiah and to those who are with him in Israel; for the Lord shall speak of this joy unto His chosen ones."
And though all the adversaries may surround thee, they shall be vanquished; for all the foes of righteousness shall gather against thee, yet for the sake of truth, go forth before them.
The Lord shall grant thee strength; as the day of trial draws near, so shall thou proceed in the power of thy Creator, neither turning to the right nor to the left, thus saith He.
And when Baruch had spoken these words, he took the scroll and went forth; and he went to Babylon and sat down in a place that was desolate, beneath a tree outside the city.

Until Jeremiah had finished speaking, the other relatives had not departed; and Jeremiah said, "Give me a place to bury my dead among my relatives," and he was granted this, and the people passed by to bury their dead there.
And as they were burying the dead, they came before him.

And he stood there and cried out with a loud voice, saying, "O Lord, You have chosen Jeremiah; to You I shall speak; go and gather all the people; until they hear the good tidings that I bring, let them come here."
And Jeremiah, having heard this, gave thanks to the Lord; and at that time, he gathered all the people, their wives, and their children; and they came to the place where he was.
And they were filled with joy and were strengthened; and death arose; and because of what was done, all the people believed and were encouraged.
And they said, "Behold, our God, who was seen by our fathers in the wilderness with Moses; this is He; today, He is the one who has been seen by us in a great vision."
And the scroll said to Jeremiah, "Come, lift this scroll and read it to the people." And he read it to the people.
And when the people heard, they all became one and were filled with joy; and they looked upon themselves and said to Jeremiah, "What shall we do to enter our land? Let us speak."
And Jeremiah arose and said, "As you have heard in the scroll, so shall you do, and it shall return to your land."

Jeremiah also wrote a letter to Baruch, saying, “My son and my beloved, until we depart from the command of the sinful king, let us not cease to pray for our land, that it may be guided by our God, and do not be weary in our supplications for us.”
But you, when you come from Babylon, shall not be found among those who have returned, for you have found favor in the sight of God.
As a father has a son, so shall the son be rewarded; and those who are with their father shall not see his sorrow, lest they hide their faces.

Thus, your God shall have mercy upon you; and we, from the time we arrived in this land until this day, have not ceased from sorrow, and that we may not see the affliction of the people, you shall not return to Babylon.
And to the king and to the nobles, they cried out, saying, “O Lord, God of the heavens, have mercy upon us,” and we found them among the people.
Indeed, those who have oppressed you, when they call upon another god, saying, “Have mercy upon us,” I wept when I heard this.
And again, I remembered the feast that was held in Jerusalem; and as I pondered this, I was filled with sorrow and was returning to my house.

Now, let them hear my voice as they depart from the land of the Persians, and let them receive what has come forth from my mouth concerning our brethren Abimelech and you, where you dwell, our Creator.
Now, in this time of our distress, let us say, “Your Creator, who is praised in Zion, let us speak of a new praise,” and I shall tell you this.
And we said, “How shall we sing the Lord's song in a strange land?” They did not answer us.
And Jeremiah wrote a letter, saying, "Go in peace; the Lord shall be with you."
And he took the letter and went forth; and he delivered the letter to Baruch; and Baruch read the letter aloud, and when he heard the sorrow and affliction of the people, he wept.
But Jeremiah received that which was given to him and delivered it to the people, as he was commanded.
He also sat down to instruct the nations of Babylon, that they should not commit evil.
And the Lord, when the day came for His people to be delivered from Babylon,
said to Jeremiah, "Arise; and let your brethren arise; and go to the Jordan; for the Lord shall deliver the people from the work of the Babylonians."

"Let the women be taken from among you, and the men also; and let the women be taken captive; and those who have heard your word, let them return to Jerusalem; but those who have not heard you, let them go to her that they may not be taken."

And Jeremiah read all these words to them; and he brought them to the Jordan; and when the Lord spoke to them, the people were diverse; and they did not wish to be taken; and they did not listen to Jeremiah.
And there were those who said, "We will take our wives for eternity; we shall bring them with us to our land," and they departed from the Jordan and came to Jerusalem.
And Jeremiah and Baruch, and Abimelech said, "Every man who takes a woman from Babylon shall not enter our land," and they arose.
And the women who had been taken captive said to their husbands, “Arise; let us return to Babylon,” and they went back to Babylon.

And when the men of Babylon saw them, they came forth to receive them; saying, “You have wronged us, for you have gone away from us and have taken our women and children,” and they did not let them return to Babylon.
“Because you have gone away from us, we declare in the name of our God that you shall not receive our women and children,” they said to them.
Thus they heard the word and returned to Jerusalem; and they established a city in Jerusalem, which is called Samaria.

And Jeremiah sent to them, saying, “Enter into peace; behold, the angel of righteousness shall come to you; he shall return you to the place where you dwell for many days,” and they rejoiced greatly, and for the sake of the people they made offerings and remained seven days.
And after this was done, on the tenth day, Jeremiah went out alone.
And Jeremiah prayed, saying, “O Holy One, who art good and dost reveal knowledge unto me, until thou dost come unto me, thou art the true and wise one.”

Concerning thy kindred, concerning Israel, I will give thanks; concerning the beloved, concerning the Seraphim, I will give thanks for the good and holy ones; concerning the Cherubim, I will give thanks; for Michael, the chief of the righteous angels, is truly worthy of my praise; he who enlightens me, and who opens the gates of righteousness unto the righteous until they enter therein.

O Lord of all, I give thanks; thou art the Lord who possessest all; thou hast created all that is seen and unseen; all that hath been made, all that hath been taken captive, all that hath existed without creation, is in thee.

And he prayed thus; and after he had finished his prayer, Jeremiah entered into the temple and stood; and Baruch and Abimelech were with him; and Jeremiah's soul was as if it had been separated from his body, as one man.
And it came to pass that Baruch and Abimelech cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Woe unto us! The priest of God, our father Jeremiah, has departed from us."

And the people heard this and ran unto him; and they found Jeremiah as one who was dead and mourned for him; and they tore their garments; and upon themselves was a great lamentation; they mourned bitterly.
And when they prepared for him, there came a word saying, "It is well, for his soul shall return to his body, and do not grieve."
And when they heard this word, they waited three days around him, until his soul returned to his body, but they did not grieve.
And in the midst of all, a voice was heard saying, "In one accord give thanks; give thanks to our God; and all of you give thanks to the Son of God, our Savior."
The light of the world, the Son of God, Jesus, shall judge you.
It is an unquenchable light, and it is the life of faith.
After this time, to come to the earth shall be three hundred thirty-three days.
"In the midst of paradise stands the tree of life, which has not been planted; it causes all trees to bear fruit, and those who are withered shall come unto it."
It causes them to bear fruit, to blossom, and to flourish; that the earth may not be barren, let us offer our service to the heavenly God; the color of crimson shall be as a sign of the covenant.

The water that is bitter shall become sweet; and the bitterness shall become sweet. And the son shall gather the fruit of the vine, for the Lord shall rejoice with great joy and delight in the islands.

He shall come into this world as a man; I have seen him as a man, sent from the Father to this world; and he shall come into this world as a man, that he may be seen by them, and that he may reveal to them twelve apostles for himself; and he shall go to the mount of olives; and all our souls that are weary shall be refreshed.
And as he comes into this world, Jeremiah spoke concerning the Son of God, saying thus.

And when the people heard this, Jeremiah said, "I have seen the Son of God," and because of what was spoken, they were troubled; and behold, they said, "As we have done in Isaiah, let us also do to him; arise." And they said, "Let us not go and harm him, but it shall not be so."
And Baruch and Abimelech cried out, saying, "Do not kill him with this death"; and Baruch and Abimelech mourned for Jeremiah.
And the chief men did not abandon the hidden secrets they had seen; and Jeremiah said to them, "As long as you instruct me in all that you have seen, you cannot kill me, so do not abandon me."
"Now bring me a stone," he said; and they brought him a stone; and he stood and said, "O light of the world, make this stone like me."
And at that time the stone resembled Jeremiah; and they began to strike the stone as if it were Jeremiah, and they committed iniquity.
But Jeremiah revealed all the secrets he had seen to Baruch and Abimelech; and he spoke to them this, and after he had finished, he went to eat, and he stood among the people.
And at that time the stone cried out, "O you children of Israel, why do you strike Jeremiah with the stone? Behold, Jeremiah is among you, and he is your life," he cried out.

And when they saw Jeremiah, they came with much stone and ran unto him; and he bore witness against them; and Baruch and Abimelech came and took him; and they brought a stone and set it at his mouth as a seal, and they dwelt there.
"Behold, this is the stone of Jeremiah's help," they wrote within themselves; and behold, the matter concerning Jeremiah is that it has been written in the book of Baruch.
